title: Post COVID-19 vaccination neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder: Case report & MRI findings
case_prompt:
A 34-year-old man with no significant medical history presented with a 2-week history of acute confusion, imbalance, headache, and dizziness. He denied fever, loss of consciousness, seizures, or sensory loss and had no history of trauma or similar prior episodes. He received two doses of the Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine, with the second dose 3 weeks before presentation. 

On examination, he was hemodynamically stable and afebrile but confused, disoriented to person and place, able to follow only one-step commands, and occasionally provided irrelevant answers. There were no signs of skin or joint involvement. Neurologic examination revealed bilateral proptosis; cranial nerves, sensation, muscle power, and tone were otherwise normal in all four limbs. Gait was ataxic.

Laboratory studies showed a normal complete blood count. Viral PCR testing for SARS-CoV-2, adenovirus, HSV-1 and ‑2, EBV, CMV, and HIV was negative. CSF analysis demonstrated lymphocytic pleocytosis and mildly elevated protein; cultures, cytology, oligoclonal bands, antibodies to HSV, syphilis antigens, cryptococcal antigen, and VZV were all negative. Autoimmune serologies (thyroid antibodies, ANCA, rheumatoid factor, anticardiolipin) and vitamin levels were normal. SARS-CoV-2 IgG was positive. 

A brain MRI with FLAIR sequencing revealed patchy hyperintense signal along the ependymal surfaces of the lateral, third, and fourth ventricles, the periaqueductal gray matter, thalamus, corpus callosum, and optic chiasm. A cervical spine MRI was normal.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Acute disseminated encephalomyelitis was initially suspected due to recent vaccination but was reconsidered after imaging suggested NMO — “the patient was admitted under the care of the neurology team as a suspected case of acute disseminated encephalomyelitis in view of the history of recent vaccination.” … “The MRI findings were suggestive of neuromyelitis optica and aquaporin-4 serum autoantibody was ordered accordingly…”  
2. Multiple sclerosis was considered among post-vaccination white matter diseases but was made unlikely by negative oligoclonal bands — “CSF analysis were negative for ... oligoclonal bands ...”  
3. Guillain–Barré syndrome was included in the differential of post-vaccination demyelination but was excluded by preserved strength and sensation — “Neurologic examination showed ... intact sensory, and muscle power and tone in 4 limbs.”  
4. Neuro–Behçet disease was considered in the setting of post-vaccination white matter involvement but was excluded by absence of skin or joint findings — “There were no signs of skin or joint involvement.”
